creative_intent: Generate a simple geometric test render focusing on a clean matte B4C technical ceramic sphere against a black background, prioritizing material study.

must_have: clearly readable contour of a manufactured sphere
unambiguous evidence of a single, solid, engineered object
exactly one manufactured object as the clear subject
visible contour evidence such as edge, rim, bevel, seam, or curvature
material visibly attached to the object, not floating as texture

constraints: avoid harsh shadows that obscure material detail
ensure uniform illumination across the visible surface
color must remain subordinate to material identity
color must follow form then material, never override them
no flat color, always material texture variation
pure white and pure black are forbidden
ceramic off-white must stay warm and broken, never sterile pure white
charcoal black must keep temperature variation, never dead pure black
restrained crimson only in seams, cores, or controlled heat accents
muted earth support only, low saturation material support tones

core_risks: abstract drift, losing the manufactured object read
loss of clear object silhouette or contour
material misread as plaster, stone, or glossy plastic
anti_drift_rules: lock the object read as a singular, manufactured B4C technical ceramic sphere
prevent any abstract, atmospheric, or non-object interpretations
maintain a material-only scope without losing the manufactured object's readability
suppress all forbidden material reads explicitly
always preserve one clearly readable manufactured object
do not let texture or atmosphere become the subject
keep material identity locked and explicit
form -> material -> color priority is mandatory
do not allow neon, pure white, pure black, or plastic-clean RGB drift
crimson may appear only as restrained seam/core accent when applicable
success_criteria: clear, unambiguous read of a matte B4C technical ceramic surface
the object is clearly identifiable as a manufactured sphere
absence of all forbidden material reads
strong subject presence and clear manufactured object read
image does not collapse into abstract texture or atmosphere
color feels subtractive and pigment-like, never RGB-clean
shadow mass dominates and color remains materially grounded
direction_summary: Prioritize a clean, matte B4C technical ceramic material read on a clearly manufactured sphere, presented against a black background. Maintain material-only scope while ensuring the object's identity and contour are unambiguous.
